title: Low volatility, the calmer half
author: arhancanli
rationale: Calmer stocks have historically earned about as much as wilder ones, against what simple theory predicts, possibly because some investors overpay for lottery-like shares.
risks: Lags in sharp rallies, and tends to crowd into a few sectors such as utilities and staples, so it carries interest rate exposure.
references: Ang, Hodrick, Xing and Zhang (2006), The Cross-Section of Volatility and Expected Returns, Journal of Finance
Blitz and van Vliet (2007), The Volatility Effect, Journal of Portfolio Management
